metadata.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
metadata.abstract: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.
